query: How does resolution time vary across category, priority, and assignment group?

per_column.name: resolution_time_hours
per_column.rationale: This is simply the focus variable (resolution_time) expressed in hours. It restates the focus rather than providing an external associational variable to segment on. Its continuous, highly fine-grained values (many distinct floats) also make it unusable as an interpretable grouping dimension.

per_column.name: priority_level
per_column.rationale: Priority is already present in the original table and is one of the query's stated grouping dimensions. This column merely re-encodes existing priority as a numeric level, adding no external relationship not already available.

per_column.name: priority_category
per_column.rationale: A label-mapped version of the existing priority field (High/Critical/Moderate). While it has clean, well-separated categories, it is a redundant restatement of an original column that the query already names, not a newly opened associational variable.

judge.rationale: None of the added columns introduce a new external, associational dimension to explore against resolution_time. resolution_time_hours is a direct restatement of the focus (and too fine-grained to segment on), while priority_level and priority_category merely re-encode the existing priority column, which is already a grouping variable in the query. No new interpretable relationships (e.g., time-of-day, reassignment counts, caller department, SLA breach flags) are opened up, so the set fails the exploratory-analysis claim.
